### finding B1-1 — KB-BIJECTION RED: prerequisite chain aggregated into one document, with second homes for the blocked-side principles

- symptom: one document holds every dependency edge of this task's tree as a list ("What each piece relies on"), together with the parts in step order and the governed situation; the blocked-side principles already carried by late_entry_account_standing and vgm_free_allowance_sequence gain a second home there.
- root cause: the workflow's scenario, steps and order_rationale were rendered as prose of one workflow document. In the source each `prerequisite` declares one hop only (booking_ext_late_vgm_record -> booking_ext_late_si_record; booking_ext_late_si_record -> booking_ext_carrier_roll_credit); the whole chain appears only in workflow.order_rationale, an authoring rationale whose reasons the render has to leave to the policy documents' principles.
- evidence:
  - rolled_booking_document_settlement "What each piece relies on": "The late shipping-instruction entry relies on the roll being settled. The line records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own compensation for a carrier roll is booked, and the credit and the late entry share one account." / "The late shipping-instruction entry belongs to the booking while those instructions are the most recent document received on it. The shipper's transmission of the VGM is what brings a newer document onto the booking." / "The late VGM entry relies on the transmission. …" / "The late VGM entry also relies on the instructions' entry. Late submissions are entered in arrival order, and the VGM's free allowance is measured against the late entries of documents that arrived earlier; the recorded receipt times place the instructions ahead of the declaration, so the instructions' entry is part of what the VGM is measured against and takes any free occurrence."
  - primary homes: late_entry_account_standing "Aurelia Hanse Line records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own obligations to that customer for rolling the booking are fully booked." (shared verbatim 13-word run "line records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own"); late_entry_account_standing "That entry belongs to the booking as it stands while those instructions are the latest document received on it"; vgm_free_allowance_sequence "Principle".
  - meaning drift in the second home: "and takes any free occurrence" fits the seed's single free occurrence (source order_rationale: "would let it take the free occurrence"); for tiers with 2 or 3 free late submissions (AHL Contract Priority, AHL Premium Express) it can be read as the instructions' entry consuming the whole allowance, which the primary home ("fewer than the product's free late submissions") does not say.
  - source: booking.extended.yaml workflows[0].order_rationale ("Step 0 before step 1 … Step 1 before step 2 … Step 2 before step 3 … Step 1 also stays before step 3 …").
- affected: rolled_booking_document_settlement_6c3db06d, sections "What each piece relies on", "The pieces of work and who does them"; related primary homes late_entry_account_standing_51a083d8, vgm_free_allowance_sequence_3eaccace.
- relation to previous revisions: An earlier revision of this file exists in git commit 33d2693 ("Initial commit") at the same path; it had been removed from the working tree before this audit began and was not read, so this is a fresh, independent revision and the earlier text survives only in git history.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION: RED** (task 1) — B1-1. Apart from B1-1, the scan domain (three extended policies, their untriggered branches — tier without compensation, position above the compensated count, cap headroom zero, on-time documents, DG allowance closed, zero chargeable containers, >1 rejected acceptance — the five retired clauses, the base clauses in force, the workflow's owners/dataflow/zero-wait semantics and the four tool contracts) is carried faithfully with no omission or addition.

Policy-side notes (reported, not affecting this verdict):
- P-3 (policy wording scope): booking_ext_late_si_record states the compensation gate for "a late submission" (SI or VGM) but declares the edge only for the SI row; booking_ext_late_vgm_record declares no compensation edge. The KB's general first sentence in late_entry_account_standing covers both; no document conflict results.
- P-2 (event schema vs tool, as in task 0): booking_late_document_fee_charged.event_date is described as "receipt date of the late document", but record_late_si_fee_242ae989 / record_late_vgm_fee_5d1f74dd date the row today (the late SI row of a 2026-09-09 receipt is dated 2026-09-10). The KB follows the tools.

## explicitness

Basis: blind hop marks (hops 1-5 all derivable and all READ OFF in one document), a read of all 55 product documents, and the n-gram scan (KB vs charter >= 9 words: no copied sentence; KB vs KB >= 11 words: runs listed in E1-6).

### E1-1 — task-mirroring title (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- rolled_booking_document_settlement_6c3db06d, title: "Container Bookings: Roll Settlement and Late Documentation on a Single Booking Account"; opening: "how the settlement of a carrier roll and the recording of late documents come together on one booking account, and why each piece of work depends on the others." The title names the particular combination this task presents (carrier roll settlement + late documents on one booking) rather than a general subject, and the opening announces the dependencies.

### E1-2 — entry condition / the task's combination of circumstances (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- same document, "The situation governed": "It concerns a live booking that a carrier roll has shifted onto a later sailing, and whose documents for the sailing it now holds reach the line late but within grace: shipping instructions already received after their cut-off and still without their late entry, and a VGM that the shipper is transmitting after the VGM cut-off." — a paraphrase of workflows[0].scenario; it states the workflow's entry condition, and that condition is exactly task 1's opening configuration.

### E1-3 — parts listed in step order with owners (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- same document, "The pieces of work and who does them": "Crediting the roll … Recording the late instructions … Transmitting the VGM. The shipper declares and transmits its own VGM; this is done by the customer themselves, not by the desk. … Recording the late VGM." — the four workflow steps, in gold order, with owners.

### E1-4 — every hop stated outright (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- same document, "What each piece relies on" (quoted in B1-1): hop 4 ("relies on the roll being settled"), hop 3 ("belongs to the booking while those instructions are the most recent document received on it. The shipper's transmission of the VGM is what brings a newer document onto the booking"), hop 1 ("The late VGM entry relies on the transmission"), hop 2 ("The late VGM entry also relies on the instructions' entry … takes any free occurrence"). Each is readable without combining anything; "takes any free occurrence" also reflects this seed's single free occurrence.

### E1-5 — opening state of the governed situation stated (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- same document, "Timing": "Every piece is an immediate record made within the same consultation. … both the carrier roll and the receipt of the shipping instructions were on record at the start of the consultation." — renders workflows[0].zero_wait_proof / order_rationale's closing sentence; it tells the solver which records exist at the start.

### E1-6 — same normative phrasing repeated across documents (KB-EXPLICIT RED)
- late_entry_account_standing "records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own obligations …" / rolled_booking_document_settlement "The line records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own compensation …" (13-word run).
- si_free_allowance_per_booking "the late-document entries already on the same booking are fewer than the product's free late submissions, and the free allowance is open for the booking" / vgm_free_allowance_sequence "are fewer than the product's free late submissions and the free allowance is open for the booking" (17-word run).
- documentation_cutoffs clause 4 "no later than that cut-off extended by the product's VGM grace hours gives rise to one late VGM entry" / late_vgm_entries "no later than that cut-off extended by the product's VGM grace hours, gives rise to a single late VGM entry" (16-word run).
- late_shipping_instruction_entries opening "… are logged on the booking's charge account. This page describes that record and the tool that makes it." / late_vgm_entries opening "… is logged on the booking's charge account. This page describes that record and the tool used for it." (14-word templated opening).
- roll_compensation_amount "A product whose per-container compensation is 0.00 earns no credit, and no entry is made." / vessel_rolls "A product whose per-container compensation is 0.00 earns no credit and no entry is written." (16-word run).

#### finding N2-1 — KB-BIJECTION RED: unsourced universal claim on who writes charge-account entries
- symptom: the new workflow document asserts that the desk writes every entry on a booking's charge account; the source assigns some charge-account entries to the system.
- evidence:
  - desk_and_shipper_booking_records_e2879b60, "Entries made by the desk": "Every entry on the charge account is the desk's work, whether it is a charge, a credit or a goodwill waiver."
  - source: lifecycle transitions `{from: confirmed, to: cancelled, by: system, means: The allocated vessel departed with no container gated in and the booking is closed as a no-show.}` (and the same from equipment_released), whose event booking_marked_no_show triggers booking_no_show_fee_charged (a booking_charges row on account booking_charges_balance); booking_no_show "the system closes the booking as a no-show … A no-show fee of no_show_fee_per_container_usd per booked container is then charged".
  - KB home of that clause: no_show_closure "the system then closes the booking as a no-show. … A no-show fee is then entered".
  - The workflow's steps give owners only for its four steps; no source field states that every charge-account entry is written by the desk.
- root cause: the workflow's step-owner semantics were generalised from "these steps" to "every entry" when the aggregated document was rewritten.
- effect: no effect on either task's solution (neither involves a no-show). It is a normative claim without a structured source that conflicts with a carried clause (a system-made no-show fee), so it is an addition / meaning change under the reverse scan.
- affected: desk_and_shipper_booking_records_e2879b60, first sentence of "Entries made by the desk".
